patterns.reflex: Reflex drills (syntax you must type without thinking)

drills.title: Letter counts with int[26]
drills.statement:
Return an int[26] where index 0 holds how many times 'a' appears in s, index 1 'b', and so on.
Count only lowercase letters a-z; ignore everything else (uppercase, digits, punctuation).

Example: letterCounts("hello") -> count['l' - 'a'] == 2

drills.title: Valid Anagram
drills.statement:
Return true if t is an anagram of s (same letters, same counts). Both contain only lowercase a-z.

Example: ("anagram", "nagaram") -> true, ("rat", "car") -> false

drills.title: Valid Palindrome
drills.statement:
Return true if s reads the same forwards and backwards after lowercasing and removing every
character that is not a letter or digit.

Example: "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama" -> true, "race a car" -> false

drills.title: Word frequency with HashMap.merge
Max Sum of k Consecutive
drills.statement:
Return the maximum sum of any k consecutive elements (1 <= k <= n). Return a long.
Must be O(n): one test has n = 1,000,000 and k = 500,000.

Example: [1, 4, 2, 10, 23, 3, 1, 0, 20], k = 4 -> 39

drills.title: Range Sum Queries
drills.statement:
Each query is {l, r}. Return a long[] with the sum of a[l..r] (inclusive) for every query.
Must be O(n + q): one test has 200,000 numbers and 200,000 queries.

drills.title: Grouping with computeIfAbsent
Binary Search
drills.statement:
a is sorted ascending with distinct values. Return the index of x, or -1. Must be O(log n).

Example: [-1, 0, 3, 5, 9, 12], x = 9 -> 4

drills.title: Valid Parentheses
drills.statement:
s contains only ()[]{}. Return true if every bracket is closed by the same type, in the
correct order.

Example: "()[]{}" -> true, "([)]" -> false, "{[]}" -> true

drills.title: Comparator chaining
drills.statement:
Return a NEW list of the people sorted by age ascending, then by name alphabetically
when ages are equal. Do not modify the input list.

drills.title: Number of Islands
drills.statement:
grid has '1' (land) and '0' (water). An island is land connected up/down/left/right.
Return the number of islands. You may modify the grid.
One test is a 1000 x 1000 island - recursive DFS will overflow the stack. Use BFS with a queue.

drills.title: Merge Intervals
drills.statement:
Merge all overlapping intervals and return them sorted by start. Intervals that only touch
([1,4] and [4,5]) also merge. The input is NOT sorted.

Example: [[1,3],[2,6],[8,10],[15,18]] -> [[1,6],[8,10],[15,18]]

drills.title: Sorting int[][] safely
drills.statement:
Sort the pairs IN PLACE by first value ascending; when first values tie, by second value
DESCENDING. Return the same array. Values can be anywhere in the int range - a comparator
that uses subtraction will overflow and fail.

drills.title: Climbing Stairs
drills.statement:
You can climb 1 or 2 steps at a time. Return the number of distinct ways to reach step n (n >= 1)
as a long. n goes up to 90, so plain recursion is far too slow.

Example: n = 3 -> 3 (1+1+1, 1+2, 2+1)

drills.title: Top K Frequent Elements
drills.statement:
Return the k most frequent values (any order). The answer is guaranteed to be unique.

Example: [1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3], k = 2 -> [1, 2]

drills.title: Binary search skeleton
drills.statement:
a is sorted ascending (duplicates allowed). Return the first index i with a[i] >= x,
or a.length if every element is smaller than x. Must be O(log n).

Example: a = [1, 3, 3, 5]: x=3 -> 1, x=4 -> 3, x=6 -> 4

drills.title: Run-Length Compression
drills.statement:
Replace each run of the same character with the character followed by the run length.
Runs of length 1 are written as just the character.

Example: "aaabcc" -> "a3bc2", "aaaaaaaaaaaa" -> "a12", "aabbaa" -> "a2b2a2"

drills.title: Two Sum (unsorted)
Prefix sum array
drills.statement:
prefix(a) returns a long[] of length n + 1 where pre[i] = a[0] + ... + a[i-1] (pre[0] = 0).
rangeSum(pre, l, r) returns a[l] + ... + a[r] (inclusive) in O(1).
Use long: sums can exceed the int range.

drills.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
drills.statement:
nums is sorted ascending. Remove duplicates IN PLACE so each value appears once in the first k
positions (in order), and return k. What is left after position k does not matter.

Example: [0,0,1,1,1,2,2,3,3,4] -> k = 5, nums starts with [0,1,2,3,4]

drills.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
drills.statement:
Return the length of the longest substring of s with no repeated characters.

Example: "abcabcbb" -> 3 ("abc"), "bbbbb" -> 1, "pwwkew" -> 3
Watch out for "abba": the left edge must never move backwards.

drills.title: Split, reverse, join
drills.statement:
Reverse the order of the words in s. Words are separated by one or more spaces; the result
has single spaces between words and no leading/trailing spaces.

Example: "  the sky  is blue " -> "blue is sky the"

drills.title: Find Pivot Index
drills.statement:
Return the leftmost index i where the sum of everything strictly left of i equals the sum of
everything strictly right of i, or -1. (An empty side sums to 0.)

Example: [1, 7, 3, 6, 5, 6] -> 3; [1, 2, 3] -> -1; [2, 1, -1] -> 0

drills.title: First and Last Position
drills.statement:
a is sorted ascending (duplicates allowed). Return {first, last} index of x, or {-1, -1}.
Must be O(log n) per call.

Example: [5, 7, 7, 8, 8, 10], x = 8 -> {3, 4}
Hint: two lower-bound searches: lowerBound(x) and lowerBound(x + 1) - 1.

drills.title: PriorityQueue min-heap of size k
drills.statement:
Return the k-th largest element of a (1-based: k = 1 is the maximum). Duplicates count
separately. Use a min-heap that never holds more than k elements.

Example: [3, 2, 1, 5, 6, 4], k = 2 -> 5

drills.title: Daily Temperatures (next greater element)
drills.statement:
For each day i, out[i] = how many days until a strictly warmer temperature, or 0 if never.
Must be O(n): one test has 100,000 days.

Example: [73, 74, 75, 71, 69, 72, 76, 73] -> [1, 1, 4, 2, 1, 1, 0, 0]
Hint: a stack of indices still waiting for a warmer day (monotonic stack).

drills.title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
drills.statement:
n x n grid of 0 (open) and 1 (blocked). Moving in any of the 8 directions, return the length of
the shortest path from top-left to bottom-right counted in CELLS (start and end included),
or -1 if there is none (including when start or end is blocked).

Example: [[0,1],[1,0]] -> 2

drills.title: BFS on a grid
drills.statement:
grid[r][c] is '.' (open) or '#' (wall). Starting at (sr, sc), return an int[R][C] with the
minimum number of 4-directional steps to every cell. Walls and unreachable cells get -1.

drills.title: Meeting Rooms II
drills.statement:
Each interval is {start, end}. Return the minimum number of rooms needed so no two meetings
share a room at the same time. A meeting ending at 5 frees the room for one starting at 5.

Example: [[0,30],[5,10],[15,20]] -> 2
Hint: sort by start; a min-heap holds end times of rooms in use.

drills.title: Coin Change (fewest coins)
drills.statement:
Return the fewest coins needed to make amount, using unlimited coins of each value, or -1 if
it cannot be made. amount = 0 needs 0 coins.

Example: coins [1, 2, 5], amount 11 -> 3 (5 + 5 + 1)

drills.title: BufferedReader + StringTokenizer
drills.statement:
input looks exactly like HackerRank stdin: the first line is n, the second line holds n
integers separated by one or more spaces. Return their sum as a long.
Read it with BufferedReader (over a StringReader) and StringTokenizer - the same code you
would write in main() with System.in.

Example: "3\n1 2 3\n" -> 6

drills.title: K Closest Points to Origin
drills.statement:
Return the k points closest to (0, 0) by Euclidean distance (any order). The answer is unique.
Coordinates can be large: x*x + y*y overflows an int - compare squared distances as long.

Example: [[3,3],[5,-1],[-2,4]], k = 2 -> [[3,3],[-2,4]]

drills.title: Caesar Cipher
drills.statement:
Shift every letter k places through the alphabet, wrapping around and keeping its case.
Non-letters stay the same. k can be negative or larger than 26.

Example: ("Hello, World!", 5) -> "Mjqqt, Btwqi!", ("abc", -1) -> "zab"
Hint: Math.floorMod handles negative shifts.

drills.title: Two pointers on a sorted array
First Unique Character
drills.statement:
Return the index of the first character in s that appears exactly once, or -1 if none.
s contains only lowercase a-z.

Example: "leetcode" -> 0, "loveleetcode" -> 2, "aabb" -> -1

drills.title: 3Sum
drills.statement:
Return every unique triplet [a, b, c] of values from nums (different indices) with a + b + c == 0.
No duplicate triplets. Order of triplets / order inside a triplet does not matter.
Must be O(n^2): one test has 3,000 numbers.

Example: [-1, 0, 1, 2, -1, -4] -> [[-1, -1, 2], [-1, 0, 1]]
Hint: sort, fix the first value, two-pointer the rest, skip repeated values.

drills.title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
drills.statement:
All numbers are positive. Return the length of the shortest contiguous subarray whose sum is
>= target, or 0 if there is none. Must be O(n): one test has 1,000,000 numbers.

Example: target 7, [2, 3, 1, 2, 4, 3] -> 2 ([4, 3])

drills.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
drills.statement:
Return how many contiguous subarrays sum to exactly k. Numbers can be negative, so a sliding
window does NOT work. Return a long - the answer can exceed the int range.
Must be O(n): one test has 200,000 numbers.

Example: [1, 1, 1], k = 2 -> 2; [1, -1, 0], k = 0 -> 3
Hint: prefix sums + a HashMap counting how often each prefix sum has appeared.

drills.title: Integer Square Root
drills.statement:
Return floor(sqrt(x)) for x >= 0 WITHOUT Math.sqrt or Math.pow.
Binary search on the answer - and watch out: mid * mid overflows an int.

Example: 8 -> 2, 2147395599 -> 46339

drills.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
drills.statement:
Evaluate an expression in Reverse Polish Notation. Tokens are integers (possibly negative,
like "-11") or one of + - * /. Division truncates toward zero (Java's normal int division).
The expression is always valid.

Example: ["2", "1", "+", "3", "*"] -> 9

drills.title: Rotting Oranges (multi-source BFS)
drills.statement:
0 = empty, 1 = fresh orange, 2 = rotten orange. Every minute, fresh oranges next to a rotten one
(up/down/left/right) become rotten. Return the minutes until no fresh orange is left, or -1 if
some fresh orange can never rot.

Example: [[2,1,1],[1,1,0],[0,1,1]] -> 4
Hint: put ALL rotten oranges in the queue at the start, then BFS level by level.

drills.title: Non-overlapping Intervals
drills.statement:
Return the minimum number of intervals to remove so the rest do not overlap.
Touching intervals ([1,2] and [2,3]) do NOT overlap.

Example: [[1,2],[2,3],[3,4],[1,3]] -> 1
Hint: sort by END time and greedily keep the interval that finishes first.

drills.title: House Robber
drills.statement:
You cannot take money from two adjacent houses. Return the maximum total you can take.
Must be O(n): one test has 100,000 houses.

Example: [2, 7, 9, 3, 1] -> 12 (2 + 9 + 1); [2, 1, 1, 2] -> 4

drills.title: Merge K Sorted Arrays
drills.statement:
Each array is sorted ascending (some may be empty). Return one sorted array with every element.
Aim for O(N log k) with a min-heap holding one "next element" per array.

Example: [[1,4,5],[1,3,4],[2,6]] -> [1,1,2,3,4,4,5,6]

drills.title: Longest Common Prefix
drills.statement:
Return the longest prefix shared by every string in the array ("" if none or if the array is empty).

Example: [flower, flow, flight] -> "fl"

drills.title: Group Anagrams
drills.statement:
Group the words that are anagrams of each other. Groups appear in the order their first word
appears in the input, and words inside a group keep their input order.

Example: [eat, tea, tan, ate, nat, bat] -> [[eat, tea, ate], [tan, nat], [bat]]
Hint: a sorted copy of the letters makes a good map key. LinkedHashMap keeps insertion order.

drills.title: Container With Most Water
drills.statement:
h[i] is the height of a vertical line at x = i. Pick two lines; the water they hold is
min(h[i], h[j]) * (j - i). Return the maximum. Must be O(n): one test has 100,000 lines.

Example: [1,8,6,2,5,4,8,3,7] -> 49

drills.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
drills.statement:
s has only uppercase A-Z. You may change at most k characters to any other uppercase letter.
Return the length of the longest substring that can be made of one repeated letter.

Example: "ABAB", k = 2 -> 4; "AABABBA", k = 1 -> 4
Hint: a window is valid while (window length - count of its most common letter) <= k.

drills.title: Product of Array Except Self
drills.statement:
Return out where out[i] is the product of every element except nums[i]. Do it in O(n)
WITHOUT division (think: product of everything to the left times everything to the right).
The answer always fits in an int.

Example: [1, 2, 3, 4] -> [24, 12, 8, 6]

drills.title: Koko Eating Bananas (search on the answer)
drills.statement:
piles[i] bananas in each pile. At speed k Koko eats up to k bananas from ONE pile per hour
(a pile of 7 at speed 3 takes 3 hours). Return the minimum integer k to finish all piles
within h hours (h >= piles.length). Piles go up to 1,000,000,000 - total hours can overflow
an int, and so can p + k - 1.

Example: [3, 6, 7, 11], h = 8 -> 4

drills.title: Min Stack (design a class)
drills.statement:
Implement a stack that supports push, pop, top and getMin - ALL in O(1).
pop/top/getMin are only called on a non-empty stack.

Hint: store each value together with the minimum at the time it was pushed.

drills.title: Flood Fill
drills.statement:
Starting from pixel (sr, sc), recolor it and every pixel connected to it (up/down/left/right)
that has the SAME original color, to the new color. Return the image (modify in place is fine).
Traps: if the new color equals the old one, do nothing (otherwise you loop forever), and one test
is 1000 x 1000 - recursion will overflow the stack.

drills.title: Largest Number (custom comparator)
drills.statement:
Arrange the non-negative numbers so that, concatenated, they form the largest number.
Return it as a String.

Example: [3, 30, 34, 5, 9] -> "9534330"; [0, 0] -> "0"
Hint: put a before b when (a + b) > (b + a) as strings.

drills.title: Longest Common Subsequence
drills.statement:
Return the length of the longest subsequence common to a and b (characters in order, not
necessarily contiguous). One test has two strings of length 3,000.

Example: ("abcde", "ace") -> 3
Hint: dp[i][j] = LCS of the first i chars of a and the first j chars of b.

drills.title: Last Stone Weight
drills.statement:
Repeatedly smash the two heaviest stones x <= y: if x == y both are destroyed, otherwise a stone
of weight y - x remains. Return the weight of the last stone, or 0 if none are left.

Example: [2, 7, 4, 1, 8, 1] -> 1

drills.title: String Rotation
drills.statement:
Return true if b can be obtained by rotating a (moving some prefix of a to its end).

Example: ("waterbottle", "erbottlewat") -> true, ("abc", "acb") -> false
Hint: every rotation of a appears inside a + a.

drills.title: Unique Paths with Obstacles
drills.statement:
Move only right or down from the top-left to the bottom-right cell. 1 = obstacle, 0 = open.
Return the number of distinct paths (fits in an int).

Example: [[0,0,0],[0,1,0],[0,0,0]] -> 2
